learning_objective: Understand how clients and servers communicate using HTTP requests and responses.
hands_on: Use curl to send GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE requests to a sample API and record the response codes.
expected_outcome: Explain HTTP methods, headers, request body, response body, and status codes.

learning_objective: Understand REST-style resource design and how APIs expose application functionality.
hands_on: Design REST endpoints for a todo app: create todo, list todos, update todo, delete todo.
expected_outcome: Explain resources, methods, status codes, request validation, and idempotency.

learning_objective: Understand when persistent bidirectional connections are useful.
hands_on: Build or run a tiny WebSocket echo server and connect to it from a browser client.
expected_outcome: Explain the difference between HTTP request-response and persistent WebSocket communication.

learning_objective: Understand RPC-style service communication and protocol buffers.

official_docs.title: gRPC — Core concepts, architecture and lifecycle

hands_on: Create a small proto file for a UserService with GetUser and CreateUser methods.
expected_outcome: Explain service definitions, proto files, clients, servers, unary calls, and streaming.

learning_objective: Understand relational databases, tables, rows, columns, and SQL basics.
hands_on: Create a users table, insert records, query them, and update one row.
expected_outcome: Explain tables, primary keys, SQL queries, and basic database operations.

learning_objective: Understand why indexes speed up reads but add write/storage overhead.
hands_on: Create an index on a table and compare query plans before and after using EXPLAIN.
expected_outcome: Explain why indexes help lookups and why too many indexes can hurt writes.

learning_objective: Understand how Redis is used to reduce database load and improve latency.

good_reads.title: Redis — Get started with Redis Open Source

hands_on: Use Redis SET, GET, EXPIRE, and DEL commands from redis-cli.
expected_outcome: Explain cache hits, cache misses, TTL, invalidation, and why caching is hard.

learning_objective: Understand how queues decouple producers and consumers.
hands_on: Write a simple producer that sends jobs and a consumer that processes them.
expected_outcome: Explain producers, consumers, queues, retries, dead-letter queues, and backpressure.

learning_objective: Understand the difference between proving identity and checking permissions.
hands_on: Design a simple permission matrix for admin, editor, and viewer roles.
expected_outcome: Explain login, identity, sessions, tokens, roles, permissions, and least privilege.

learning_objective: Understand how systems protect APIs from abuse and overload.
hands_on: Implement a simple in-memory token bucket rate limiter.
expected_outcome: Explain fixed window, sliding window, token bucket, and why rate limits protect reliability.

learning_objective: Understand containers, images, Dockerfiles, and local development workflows.
hands_on: Write a Dockerfile for a small Python or Node.js app and run it locally.
expected_outcome: Explain image vs container, layers, ports, volumes, and environment variables.

learning_objective: Understand how to run multi-container applications locally.
hands_on: Run an app and PostgreSQL using docker-compose.yml.
expected_outcome: Explain services, networks, volumes, environment variables, and local app dependencies.

learning_objective: Understand what Kubernetes does and why teams use it.
hands_on: Run a simple Deployment and expose it with a Service using minikube or kind.
expected_outcome: Explain Pods, Deployments, Services, ReplicaSets, and basic cluster architecture.

learning_objective: Understand how Kubernetes runs and manages application workloads.
hands_on: Create a Deployment, scale replicas, update the image, and roll back.
expected_outcome: Explain desired state, reconciliation, rolling updates, and self-healing.

learning_objective: Understand how teams automate build, test, and deployment workflows.

official_docs.title: GitHub Actions — Events that trigger workflows

hands_on: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs tests on every push.
expected_outcome: Explain pipelines, jobs, steps, runners, artifacts, secrets, and deployment gates.

learning_objective: Understand logs, metrics, traces, and why production systems need observability.
hands_on: Add structured logs to a small app and include request_id in every log line.
expected_outcome: Explain logs, metrics, traces, spans, context propagation, and telemetry pipelines.

learning_objective: Understand how traces follow a request across multiple services.
hands_on: Instrument two small services and pass a trace context between them.
expected_outcome: Explain traces, spans, parent-child relationships, trace IDs, and context propagation.

learning_objective: Understand how teams define reliability targets using SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets.
hands_on: Define one SLI and one SLO for an API endpoint.
expected_outcome: Explain SLI, SLO, SLA, error budget, and why 100% reliability is usually not the goal.

learning_objective: Understand how traffic is distributed across multiple backend instances.
hands_on: Run two backend containers and put NGINX in front of them as a load balancer.
expected_outcome: Explain round-robin, health checks, reverse proxies, sticky sessions, and failure handling.

learning_objective: Understand how engineering teams respond to production issues.
hands_on: Write a mock incident timeline for an API outage.
expected_outcome: Explain severity, incident commander, timeline, communication, mitigation, and postmortems.
